title: Epidemiological Modeling of Seasonal Influenza Through Periodic Mean-Reverting Stochastic Processes

analysis.research_question_and_background: Seasonal influenza follows annual cycles, but variation in epidemic magnitude and timing complicates preparedness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We applied periodic mean reverting stochastic differential equations (SDEs) to seven seasons of weekly Texas influenza surveillance data.
analysis.methods: Missing observations were imputed using MissForest and compared with four alternative methods.
analysis.main_results: For direct modeling, p = 1/2 achieved the lowest RMSE (712.8) and AIC (5383.0), with similar AIC for p = 2/3 (5383.2).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Each specification was evaluated for direct influenza modeling and within a susceptible, exposed, infectious, and recovered model incorporating waning immunity, where the SDE governed transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The appropriate diffusion structure depended on the epidemiological quantity modeled, supporting flexible characterization of seasonal transmission variability while requiring prospective validation before operational forecasting.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Model-based parametric bootstrap assessed direct-model parameter uncertainty.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to improve preparedness for seasonal influenza by modeling its annual cycles using periodic mean-reverting stochastic differential equations (SDEs). The researchers applied these equations to seven seasons of weekly Texas influenza surveillance data, focusing on the dynamics of transmission and epidemic variability. They imputed missing observations using MissForest and compared them with alternative methods. For direct modeling, the parameter p = 1/2 achieved the lowest RMSE and AIC, suggesting it best captured influenza variability. The study also evaluated the SDEs within a susceptible, exposed, infectious, and recovered (SEIR) model, incorporating waning immunity. The findings highlight the importance of selecting the appropriate diffusion structure based on the epidemiological quantity being modeled, which could enhance understanding of seasonal transmission patterns. However, the study emphasizes the need for prospective validation before operational forecasting. The analysis identified dependence between mean-reversion and diffusion parameters, indicating potential complexities in model interpretation. While the study provides valuable insights into modeling influenza dynamics, its results are based on historical data and may not fully account for real-time variability or external factors influencing transmission.

title: Affinity Peptide-Engineered Magnetic Microswimmers for Ultrafast On-the-Fly Screening of Influenza A Virus in Microliter-Scale Samples.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Monitoring respiratory viruses is crucial for mitigating their spread and the associated healthcare costs, especially during the cold season.

analysis.methods: The micromotors are modified with a rhodamine B-labeled peptide highly specific toward the hemagglutinin A HA1 protein antigen.
analysis.main_results: The improved fluid mixing imparted by the micromotor motion allows for efficient operation during an assay time of 1 min using just 1 μL of sample.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The developed fluorescent assay represents a reliable and robust screening platform for influenza clinical samples, achieving exceptional selectivity and limits of detection in the ng/L range.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The method’s performance was validated using nasopharyngeal specimens, demonstrating high reliability and analytical specificity for the Influenza A H3N2 subtype.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Notably, the protocol provided high fluorescence signatures for H3N2-infected samples even when cycle threshold (Ct) values were comparable to those of H1N1-infected samples and negative samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel on-the-fly fluorescence method for rapid detection of the H3N2 subtype of Influenza A virus using magnetically propelled WS2/Ni micromotors. The approach leverages a rhodamine B-labeled peptide specific to the HA1 protein antigen, enabling efficient operation with just 1 μL of sample in 1 minute. The assay demonstrates exceptional selectivity and detection limits in the ng/L range, validated with nasopharyngeal specimens. It shows high reliability and specificity for H3N2, even when Ct values are similar to those of H1N1 and negative samples. The method's performance highlights its potential as a fast, sample-to-result diagnostic platform for influenza. However, the study focuses on H3N2 and does not address other subtypes or related viruses, which are considered supplementary. The findings suggest a promising tool for improving influenza surveillance and diagnostics, particularly in resource-limited settings.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect was conducted from database inception to 1 July 2026. The clinical and methodological characteristics varied across studies; consequently, the findings were synthesized narratively. Potential population overlap was considered when synthesizing findings across publications to avoid duplicate aggregation of patient data.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). Causal inference remains limited by confounding, heterogeneity, and potentially overlapping study populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Evidence for other antivirals was limited, and one confirmed treatment-emergent H274Y neuraminidase resistance event was identified. This systematic review synthesized evidence on antiviral regimens, treatment timing, clinical and virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance in laboratory-confirmed human A(H5N1) infection.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the effectiveness of antiviral treatment for human influenza A(H5N1) infection, focusing on treatment timing, clinical outcomes, virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance. title: Rare recovery of reassortants between contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses and human influenza A viruses in vitro.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza A virus (IAV) pandemics can arise when animal-derived and human-adapted IAVs exchange genome segments; however, whether contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can generate viable reassortants with human IAVs is unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we tested the reassortment potential of two clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses with human-adapted H1N1 and H3N2 IAVs using a biosafe reassortment system.
analysis.methods: Across multiple coinfection conditions, we genotyped 2,698 plaque-purified viral clones and recovered 20 reassortants (0.74%).
analysis.main_results: Polymerase assays identified human IAV subunits, particularly H1N1 PA or H3N2 PB2, that increased H5N1 polymerase activity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Thus, contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can reassort with human IAVs, but factors beyond polymerase compatibility may limit their recovery.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that reassortment between H5N1 and human IAVs is possible, which has implications for understanding the potential for viral evolution and pandemic emergence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to in vitro conditions, and the low recovery rate of reassortants may not reflect in vivo scenarios, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Overlapping Miller Fisher Syndrome and Pharyngeal–Cervical–Brachial Variant of Guillain–Barré Syndrome Following Seasonal Influenza Vaccination: A Case Report

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to report a rare case of overlapping Miller Fisher Syndrome (MFS) and pharyngeal–cervical–brachial (PCB) variant of Guillain–Barré Syndrome (GBS) following seasonal influenza vaccination, highlighting the need to consider GBS spectrum disorders in patients with acute bulbar and oculomotor issues.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case report was conducted on a 28-year-old man with no prior medical issues who presented with neurological symptoms six days after receiving a seasonal influenza vaccine. The case involved acute bulbar impairment, marked neck weakness, and other neurological manifestations.
analysis.methods: The patient underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, nerve conduction studies, and electromyography to assess the neurological condition. Treatment included intravenous immunoglobulin and nasogastric feeding due to severe bulbar dysfunction.
analysis.main_results: The findings revealed severe acute motor denervation involving cranial, cervical, and proximal upper limb muscles, with preserved sensory responses. These results supported the diagnosis of overlapping MFS and PCB variant of GBS. The patient showed a gradual but significant recovery with mild residual imbalance and lagophthalmos at two-month follow-up.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as a rare presentation of overlapping MFS and PCB variant of GBS following influenza vaccination. They emphasized the importance of early diagnosis to manage life-threatening sequelae, even in the absence of limb weakness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The case underscores the necessity of considering GBS spectrum disorders in patients presenting with acute bulbar and oculomotor symptoms post-vaccination, which can inform clinical vigilance and management strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As a case report, the study lacks the statistical power to establish causality, and the findings are limited to a single patient. The evidence is of moderate strength due to the rarity of the condition and the absence of a control group.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a rare occurrence of overlapping Miller Fisher Syndrome (MFS) and pharyngeal–cervical–brachial (PCB) variant of Guillain–Barré Syndrome (GBS) following seasonal influenza vaccination. A 28-year-old man presented with acute bulbar impairment, neck weakness, and other neurological symptoms six days post-vaccination. Diagnostic tests confirmed the GBS spectrum disorder, and treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin and nasogastric feeding led to significant recovery. The case highlights the importance of considering GBS variants in patients with bulbar and oculomotor issues, even with preserved limb strength, and emphasizes the need for early diagnosis to prevent life-threatening complications. However, the study's limitations include its single-case design, which restricts the ability to establish causality. The evidence is of moderate strength due to the rarity of the condition and the lack of comparative data.

title: Cul4b sustains cell cycle in germinal center B cells and enables protective humoral immunity against influenza A virus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are a major public health burden, infecting millions of people worldwide. Seasonal vaccines mitigate disease, in part, by triggering the production of IAV-specific antibodies by B cells.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here we investigate the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV using mice lacking Cul4b in B cells. The study was conducted using mice as the host model.
analysis.methods: The study used mice lacking Cul4b in B cells to investigate the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV. CRL4 is critical for regulation of DNA damage responses and cell cycle maintenance, essential for B cells to mount a robust humoral response.
analysis.main_results: We found that Cul4b promoted viral clearance and anti-IAV antibody titers post-infection and immunization, and Cul4b was required for optimal vaccine-mediated protection against infectious challenge. Additionally, we found that Cul4b supports GC B cell populations and promotes their cell cycle maintenance in vivo.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We conclude that B cell intrinsic Cul4b is essential for optimal GC and antibody responses after acute IAV exposure. This study provides novel insights into the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Further investigation of CRL4 in B cells is warranted to elucidate its potential as a therapeutic target to improve vaccine efficacy. The findings may inform strategies to enhance vaccine-induced immunity against IAV.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study. The evidence strength is high as the study provides direct experimental findings on the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to IAV.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of Cul4b in B cell responses to influenza A virus (IAV) using mice lacking Cul4b in B cells. It highlights that Cul4b is essential for optimal germinal center (GC) and antibody responses after acute IAV exposure, promoting viral clearance and anti-IAV antibody titers post-infection and immunization. The findings suggest that Cul4b supports GC B cell populations and their cell cycle maintenance in vivo, which may have implications for improving vaccine efficacy against IAV. The study provides novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying B cell function in antiviral immunity, but it does not report specific limitations. The evidence strength is high due to the direct experimental findings.

title: Self-amplifying RNA vaccines encoding chimeric and mosaic hemagglutinins confer immunity against phylogenetically diverse influenza A viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Seasonal influenza vaccines require annual reformulation due to antigenic drift and provide suboptimal protection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we evaluate self-amplifying mRNA (samRNA) vaccines encoding chimeric (cHA) and mosaic (mHA) hemagglutinins representing influenza A virus HA phylogenetic groups 1 and 2.
analysis.methods: Following prime-boost immunization, group 1 cHA vaccines (cH8/1-cH5/1) elicit broad cross-reactive antibodies and confer complete protection against diverse H1N1 strains covering decades of antigenic drift.
analysis.main_results: Group 2 vaccines (cH4/3-cH15/3 and mH10/3-mH14/3) provide comparable breadth against multiple H3N2 strains and heterosubtypic H7N9 challenge, with cHA samRNA showing superior cross-group protection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Protection is associated with Fc-mediated effector functions and CD4 + T cell responses, with minimal hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing titers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Passive serum transfer confirms antibody-mediated protection independent of cellular immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Protective immunity is maintained at doses as low as 0.4 μg, demonstrating the dose-sparing advantage of the samRNA platform.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates self-amplifying RNA vaccines encoding chimeric and mosaic hemagglutinins against seasonal influenza viruses. The research addresses the need for vaccines that can provide broader protection against antigenic drift. The study demonstrates that group 1 cHA vaccines confer complete protection against diverse H1N1 strains, while group 2 vaccines offer comparable breadth against H3N2 strains and H7N9 challenge. The findings suggest that these vaccines may offer a promising approach for broadly protective influenza vaccines. The results highlight the role of Fc-mediated effector functions and CD4+ T cell responses in protection, with minimal reliance on hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing titers. The study also shows that protective immunity can be achieved at low doses, indicating a dose-sparing advantage. However, the evidence is limited to the specific vaccine formulations tested and does not address broader implications or limitations in real-world application.

title: Validation of chemical inactivation methods for Select Agent compliance using HPAIV and low-pathogenicity influenza A virus in tissues and cultured cells

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to validate chemical inactivation methods for Select Agent compliance, as the US Federal Select Agent program mandates that inactivation procedures be validated before treated materials can be removed from biocontainment for downstream use.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used HPAIV (H5N1)-infected samples to validate inactivation of material generated in cell culture, and low-pathogenicity (H1N1)-infected lung homogenates to validate inactivation of animal-derived tissues.
analysis.methods: Residual infectious virus was assessed by plaque assay and serial blind passages following inactivation. Column-based buffer exchange was used to remove cytotoxic inactivants before viability testing.
analysis.main_results: No infectious virus was detected following any of the tested conditions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results support the effectiveness of the tested inactivation methods in eliminating infectious virus, providing a framework for facility-specific validation of similar workflows.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings validate procedures for inactivating influenza A virus-containing materials, which can inform safe handling and downstream processing in biosafety settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not report limitations, but the general evidence suggests that the methods are sensitive and effective, supporting a moderate confidence in their application for inactivation validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study validates chemical inactivation methods for Select Agent compliance using HPAIV (H5N1) and low-pathogenicity influenza A (H1N1) viruses in cell culture and animal-derived tissues. No infectious virus was detected after inactivation, supporting the effectiveness of the procedures. title: Influenza Infection, Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation, and One-Year Mortality in Hospitalized Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether influenza infection increases the risk of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation (NDAF) beyond the effects of acute illness, as this association remains uncertain.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 21,653 adults hospitalized in Clalit Health Services facilities between 2012 and 2020, who underwent respiratory-virus PCR testing. The study focused on hospitalized adults with influenza A, influenza B, other respiratory viruses, and PCR-negative controls.
analysis.methods: The study used cause-specific Cox and Fine–Gray models to analyze NDAF, time-dependent Cox models for mortality, and propensity score matching for vaccination. It included time windows and excluded day-0 events.
analysis.main_results: NDAF was recorded in 1228 patients (5.7%), with 56% of cases occurring on the day of admission. No significant association was found between viral etiology and NDAF, with hazard ratios ranging from 0.73 to 1.04. However, NDAF was associated with higher one-year mortality, particularly when recorded after discharge, with a hazard ratio of 3.04.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that NDAF is a marker of increased one-year mortality, but they did not find a significant association between influenza infection or prior vaccination and NDAF.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that NDAF may be a useful indicator for predicting one-year mortality in hospitalized adults, which could inform clinical surveillance and risk assessment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's retrospective design and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in its conclusions. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on observational data and not experimental intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated whether influenza infection increases the risk of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation (NDAF) beyond acute illness effects and its association with one-year mortality. The study included 21,653 hospitalized adults tested for respiratory viruses, with influenza A, influenza B, and other viruses as exposures. NDAF was recorded in 5.7% of patients, with 56% diagnosed on admission. No significant association was found between viral etiology and NDAF, but NDAF was linked to higher one-year mortality, especially after discharge. The authors concluded that NDAF marks increased mortality risk, though the study's limitations include its observational nature and potential confounding factors. The evidence is moderate, as findings are based on retrospective data and not experimental intervention.

title: Seasonal H1N1 influenza A virus preferentially infects a pre-existing ciliogenesis-primed secretory cell state

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza A viruses (IAV) infect secretory and ciliated cells of the human airway epithelium, but whether all cells within one cell type are equally susceptible to infection remains unresolved.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of primary human bronchial epithelial cultures from three donors identified preferential infection of a transcriptionally distinct subpopulation of secretory cells by seasonal H1N1 IAV A/Hawaii/70/2019.
analysis.methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to analyze primary human bronchial epithelial cultures from three donors, identifying a transcriptionally distinct subpopulation of secretory cells preferentially infected by seasonal H1N1 IAV A/Hawaii/70/2019.
analysis.main_results: Genes upregulated in this subpopulation showed enrichment for cilium-related gene ontology terms.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results support preferential infection of ciliogenesis-primed secretory cells and refine IAV tropism beyond cell type to encompass epithelial differentiation state.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings refine our understanding of IAV tropism and suggest that epithelial differentiation state may influence susceptibility to seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ex post facto approach and small sample size, but the evidence is strong given the use of single-cell RNA sequencing and the consistency of results across three donors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the susceptibility of secretory cells to seasonal H1N1 influenza A virus infection. Using single-cell RNA sequencing on primary human bronchial epithelial cultures from three donors, the research identifies a transcriptionally distinct subpopulation of secretory cells that are preferentially infected by the virus. The results show that genes in this subpopulation are enriched for cilium-related functions, suggesting that ciliogenesis-primed secretory cells may be more susceptible to infection. The study contributes to understanding IAV tropism by highlighting the role of epithelial differentiation state in viral susceptibility. However, the ex post facto design and small sample size limit the confidence in the findings, though the evidence is considered strong due to the robust methodology and consistent results across donors.

title: Triterpenoid saponins from the aerial parts of Phytolacca americana and their anti-influenza A virus activity

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the bioactive constituents of Phytolacca americana extracts responsible for their reported anti-influenza A virus activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the crude extract and isolated saponins from Phytolacca americana using in vitro assays on H1N1-infected A549 cells.
analysis.methods: Antiviral activity was confirmed through plaque reduction and immunoblot analyses, with the plaque-assay IC50 determined to be 57.98 ± 0.26 μM.
analysis.main_results: Compound 11, a 3-O-trisaccharide phytolaccagenic acid, reduced viral NS1 RNA levels at 6 and 24 hpi in H1N1-infected A549 cells as measured by RT–qPCR.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that specific saponins from Phytolacca americana may be responsible for its antiviral activity against influenza A virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results could inform the development of novel antiviral agents derived from natural sources for the treatment of seasonal influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro assays, and the evidence is based on a single influenza strain, which may affect generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the bioactive constituents of Phytolacca americana extracts responsible for their anti-influenza A virus activity. Using in vitro assays on H1N1-infected A549 cells, the study demonstrates that compound 11, a 3-O-trisaccharide phytolaccagenic acid, reduces viral NS1 RNA levels at 6 and 24 hpi. title: Weekly dynamics, subtype replacement and regional heterogeneity of influenza activity in China, 2024-2026: A national sentinel surveillance analysis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to quantify weekly influenza dynamics in China from 2024/W01 to 2026/W21, addressing the need to characterize recent post-pandemic patterns of influenza activity, including regional timing, subtype replacement, and outbreak activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective secondary time-series analysis was performed on 125 publicly available, aggregate weekly reports from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Chinese National Influenza Center, spanning from 2024/W01 to 2026/W21.
analysis.methods: The analysis involved reconciling datasets against official reports, recalculating positivity from positive and tested specimens, and evaluating regional differences using Newey-West standard errors and cross-correlation of first-differenced weekly series.
analysis.main_results: Nationally, 1,796,636 influenza-like illness specimens were tested, with 253,219 being influenza-positive (weighted positivity, 14.1%), peaking at 49.8% in 2025/W49. Southern China had higher positivity and ILI percentages compared to Northern China, with first-difference positivity changes most strongly correlated when Northern China led Southern China by one week.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The analysis demonstrated measurable north-south temporal differences, sequential subtype replacement, and a large A(H3N2)-associated outbreak surge, highlighting the importance of explicit source-level quality control when reusing aggregated public surveillance reports.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies, particularly in understanding regional heterogeneity and the dynamics of influenza activity in China.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on aggregated public reports and the potential for inconsistencies, but the evidence is strong for regional differences and temporal dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study quantified weekly influenza dynamics in China from 2024 to 2026, revealing regional differences, subtype replacement, and a large A(H3N2) outbreak surge. The findings can inform surveillance and treatment strategies.

title: Mosaic Hemagglutinin-Based Influenza B mRNA-LNP Vaccine Induces Strong Humoral Immune Response in Non-Human Primates.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Developing broadly protective influenza vaccines remains a major challenge for global public health. The study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity of mosaic hemagglutinin-based mRNA-LNP vaccines against influenza B viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in non-human primates to compare the immunogenicity of influenza B cHA and mHA mRNA-LNP vaccines with a quadrivalent seasonal influenza virus vaccine.
analysis.methods: The researchers used lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA technology to develop the vaccines and evaluated their immunogenicity in non-human primates.
analysis.main_results: mHA mRNA-LNPs induced high binding antibody titers against antigenically distant influenza B virus strains, with significant hemagglutination inhibition and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity activity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the mHA mRNA-LNP vaccine approach could offer broader protection against influenza B viruses compared to traditional vaccines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide important insights into the development of more effective and broadly protective influenza B vaccines, which could improve global public health outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to non-human primate models and does not include human trials, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the experimental nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity of mosaic hemagglutinin (mHA)-based mRNA-LNP vaccines against influenza B viruses in non-human primates, comparing them to a quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine. The results showed that mHA mRNA-LNPs induced high binding antibody titers against antigenically distant influenza B strains, with significant hemagglutination inhibition and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity activity. These findings suggest that the mHA mRNA-LNP vaccine approach could offer broader protection against influenza B viruses, potentially improving vaccine effectiveness. However, the study is limited to non-human primate models and does not include human trials, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the experimental nature of the study.

title: Effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine against laboratory-confirmed influenza among older adults in Eastern China: A test-negative case-control study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine against laboratory-confirmed influenza in older adults in Eastern China, as evidence on its real-world effectiveness remains limited and varies by season and circulating virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A test-negative case-control study was conducted among adults aged ≥60 years attending two sentinel hospitals in Shengzhou, Zhejiang Province, during the 2025-2026 influenza season. Participants vaccinated ≥14 days before symptom onset were included in the primary analysis, while those vaccinated 0-13 days before onset were excluded.
analysis.methods: Vaccine effectiveness (VE) was calculated using multivariable logistic regression, with the adjusted odds ratio converted to a percentage by the formula (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. The study focused on estimating VE against medically attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza.
analysis.main_results: Among 532 participants in the primary analysis, 156 were influenza-positive cases and 376 were test-negative controls. Effective current-season vaccination was recorded in 32.7% of cases and 48.4% of controls.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine was associated with moderate protection against medically attended influenza in older adults under routine program conditions, which supports continued seasonal vaccination and multi-season surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide specific information on the effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine in older adults, which can inform public health strategies for seasonal influenza vaccination and surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's overall estimate remained stable across diagnostic restrictions and alternative model specifications, but subtype-specific estimates were less precise, and interaction analyses did not identify differences by age group or chronic-disease status. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine against laboratory-confirmed influenza in older adults in Eastern China using a test-negative case-control design. Among 532 participants, 156 were influenza-positive cases and 376 were test-negative controls. The vaccine was associated with moderate protection, with an adjusted VE of 46% (95% CI, 18-64) against any influenza. Type-specific VE was 42% (95% CI, 8-63) against influenza A and 60% (95% CI, 14-81) against influenza B. Subtype-specific estimates were less precise, and no differences were found by age group or chronic-disease status. The results support continued seasonal vaccination and multi-season surveillance. However, the study's evidence is moderate in strength due to limited precision in subtype-specific estimates and lack of identified interactions.

title: Pediatric Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against Emergency Visits and Hospitalization in Canada: 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza causes substantial morbidity in children, yet Canadian data on influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in preventing emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations are limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study used a test-negative case-control design. It was conducted at fourteen Canadian pediatric tertiary-care hospitals participating in the Surveillance Program for the Rapid IdeNtification and TracKing of Infectious Diseases in kidS (SPRINT-KIDS) network. Participants were symptomatic children aged 6 months to <18 years tested for influenza from October 27, 2024, to June 7, 2025, and from November 2, 2025, to June 13, 2026.
analysis.methods: VE was estimated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, epidemiologic week, site, and high-risk comorbidity.
analysis.main_results: The 2024-2025 season included 17,316 encounters (median [IQR] age=41.0 [18.5–82.3] months; 54.0% male), with 4,760 influenza-positive cases (8.9% vaccinated) and 12,556 influenza-negative controls (15.9% vaccinated). VE against any influenza was 47% (95%CI, 40–53%) in 2024-2025 and 53% (95%CI, 46–59%) in 2025-2026. VE against ED visits was 53% (95%CI, 45–59%) and 57% (95%CI, 49–63%), and VE against hospitalization was 33% (95%CI, 16–47%) and 48% (95%CI, 33–59%) in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, respectively. VE was lower against influenza A than B in both seasons.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Influenza vaccines were moderately effective against pediatric ED visits and hospitalizations in both seasons.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support continued annual influenza vaccination of children, even when substantial antigenic mismatch is anticipated.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of influenza vaccines against emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations due to influenza in Canadian children during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Using a test-negative case-control design, the research included 17,316 and 13,417 encounters across 14 pediatric hospitals. Vaccine effectiveness (VE) against any influenza was 47% and 53% in the two seasons, respectively, with higher effectiveness observed against influenza B compared to A. VE against ED visits was 53% and 57%, while against hospitalization it was 33% and 48%. The study highlights the importance of continued vaccination despite antigenic drift, particularly for influenza A. The findings are based on a robust design but do not address limitations explicitly.
